body_text: Share Alice Sewell Follow Best Packing Apps to Help You Pack for a Trip October 24, 2024 23 min read There are so many things to remember when preparing for a trip, it can be easy to forget something if you’re not organized, and few things ruin the excitement of a trip like realizing you’ve left something important at home. No matter what kind of adventure you’re heading off on, having a well-organized packing list is essential to avoid spending the start of your trip replacing what you forget instead of starting making memories. Making a digital packing list is a game-changer because it ensures you have everything you need without the stress of second-guessing yourself. Personally, I learned this the hard way. On a trip to the beach, I was so sure I had packed everything, but after landing, I realized I’d forgotten my swimsuit — a pretty essential item for a beach vacation! I spent my first afternoon shopping for a replacement instead of relaxing by the ocean. Since then, I’ve switched to using a digital packing list, and it’s made all the difference. Digital lists are easy to update, customizable for different types of trips, and accessible from almost anywhere, so there’s no chance of losing them. Plus, most packing apps let you check off items as you pack them, which has saved me from those “Did I pack that?” panic moments. Having a digital list ensures I never forget key items again — like that swimsuit! The 5 Best Packing List Apps Overall Best Packing List App: PackPoint (Free; $3.99/year iOS, $2.99/year Android) 4.7 stars on iOS (279 reviews) 4 stars on Android (40,600 reviews) Best for Overall Travel: Wanderlog (Free; $39.99) 4.9 stars on iOS (19,100 reviews) 4.6 stars on Android (18,800 reviews) Best for Specialty and Custom Packing Lists: Packr (Free; $3.49 per month/$24.99 per year/$34.99 lifetime) 4.6 stars on iOS (6,300 reviews) Best for Detailed Packing Lists: Packing Pro ($3.99) 4.8 stars on iOS (127 reviews) Best for Multiple Traveler Packing Lists: Packtor (Free) Desktop Only Apps PackPoint Wanderlog Packr Packing Pro Packtor Essentials Packing Lists ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Specialty Packing Lists ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Editable Packing Lists ✓ (with paid-for version) ✓ ✓ (with paid-for version) ✓ ✓ Sharing/exporting features ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Group Packing ✓ ✓ ✓ To-Do Lists ✓ ✓ Added Travel Planning Features or Integration With Travel Planning Apps ✓ ✓ ✓ Weather Information ✓ ✓ Free Version ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ iOS availability ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ Android availability ✓ ✓ iOS rating 4.7/5 stars 4.9/5 stars 4.6/5 stars 4.8/5 stars n/a Android rating 4/5 stars 4.6/5 stars n/a n/a n/a # of iOS reviews 279 19,100 6,300 127 n/a # of Android reviews 40,600 18,800 n/a n/a n/a Overall Best Packing List App: PackPoint PackPoint via Apple App Store : Free/$3.99; 4.7/5 stars (279 reviews) PackPoint via Google Play Store : Free/$2.99; 4/5 stars (40,600 reviews) Image Courtesy of PackPoint via Apple App Store How To Create a Packing List With PackPoint Open the PackPoint packing list app and input: Travel destination Start date of the trip Length of the trip Whether your trip is for business or pleasure Your gender The types of activities you will be doing and other packing list categories chosen from the following: Swimming Snow Sports Working Camping Gym Photography International Beach Baby Hiking Bicycling Running Fancy Dinner Motorcycling Check if you want to repeat “basics” and if you are going to do laundry on the trip. Checking these will reduce the number of common basics (underwear, socks, casual shirts, and casual pants) on your packing list — a great feature if you want to pack as light as possible. Select “Begin Packing” to get a personalized packing list based on all the information added from the above selections. Average weather will also be shown for your dates and destination, helping you know what weather you’ll need to dress for without leaving the app. Begin selecting things you have packed from the “Essentials” list with 34 items and the “Toiletries” list with 15 items. Other packing lists will also show up based on what activities/types of trips you selected, such as things you need for a beach vacation or a business trip. You can also add custom packing list items if you have PackPoint Premium. If you want to pack more than one of any item, click the plus button on the right-hand side and choose the number of items you want on your list. If there is a pre-added item that you don’t want to pack, swipe the item left and click “Hide” Pros of PackPoint Activity-Based Packing Lists: PackPoint features lots of curated packing lists that match the activities you will be doing on the trip, ensuring you have all the gear you need for your upcoming adventure. Pack Light and Laundry Features: This packing list app can create a packing list for packing light (using the repeat basics and/or laundry option), which is ideal for those wanting to pack only a carry-on bag or generally keep the weight of their luggage down. Weather Integration: Once you’ve entered your destination and travel dates, PackPoint provides a weather overview for each day of the trip. This is very helpful when packing, especially if traveling somewhere with changeable weather, as you can decide what is necessary to pack without needing to look up the forecast elsewhere or risk arriving without suitable clothing. User-Friendly Interface: PackPoint is simple to navigate, making it a valuable tool for organizing your trip. With so much to keep track of, a user-friendly packing app can help ease the stress of getting ready and ensure you don’t forget anything important. Packing lists are sharable: Your packing list can easily be shared via SMS, WhatsApp, and email which is useful if someone you’re traveling with will need to pack similar items or if you want to access the packing list on another device. These are view-only, so you won’t be able to collaborate with anyone on a list. Premium Options Available: This packing list app offers some additional features for an affordable price of under $4. Premium features include adding custom items to pack and syncing with TripIt. Cons of PackPoint Limited Customization Features: The free version of PackPoint does not allow for much customization. You can add the number of items to pack, hide items on custom lists that you don’t want, and choose some pre-created packing lists (like those for snow sports holidays or beach vacations) but you can’t add your own specific items to pack or create custom packing lists with personalized categories. These features are only available if you pay for them which isn’t great if you’re on a tight budget and are looking for a free packing list app with as many features as possible. Collaboration: PackPoint only creates packing lists for one person. You can’t add travelers or access curated lists for multiple groups like packing lists for couples or families. This can be a drawback if you’re packing for multiple people as you can’t see everything to pack in one place and will instead have to switch between trip packing lists. No Other Travel Planning Features: PackPoint is solely a packing list app, with no options to store other things needed for travel, such as flight bookings and other booking confirmations, expense tracking, itinerary planning, or activity suggestions for your trip. This can be frustrating if you’re looking for additional travel planning features as you’ll have to switch between apps for different functions. Notable Features of PackPoint Activity-Based Packing Lists PackPoint features packing lists for “Essentials” and “Toiletries,” plus 16 other categorized packing lists related to common activities like going to the beach, going to the gym, and hiking. This feature makes it easy to create a personalized list with items needed for all the activities you will be enjoying on your trip. Pack Light Features With PackPoint, you can generate a list with new items for every day of the trip or select options that help you reduce the number of items in your luggage. The app includes a pack light feature that generates a packing list with as few items as possible and a laundry feature, which reduces the number of items based on the fact that you can wash and re-wear many things. You can also combine the two to get an even more condensed list. Weather Information After adding a location of travel and your travel dates, the average weather for each day will be shown. This includes the average temperature, a high and low temperature, and the primary type of weather for the day, such as mainly rainy or mainly sunny. It’s useful to know exactly what the weather will be like during your trip to finalize items to pack. For example, will you need a raincoat? Or should you pack extra shorts and t-shirts due to it being unseasonably hot during the trip? Sharing Options You can share your packing list with others or email it to yourself (to access on other devices). Sharing can be done via email, text message, and WhatsApp. TripIt Integration With PackPoint Pro, you can sync your packing list with TripIt which helps with itinerary planning and travel documentation storage. This is useful if you are already using that app or if you are looking for an app that helps with other travel organization on top of packing lists, allowing you to have everything you need in one place. Is PackPoint Free? Yes, PackPoint is free to download and most of the packing list app’s features are free to access. For $3.99 via the Apple App Store and $2.99 via the Google Play store, you can access additional features with a PackPoint Premium account. PackPoint Free Features Pre-created packing checklists for travel essentials and toiletries. Curated packing checklists for 16 different activities and situations: – Swimming – Snow Sports – Working – Camping – Hiking – Gym – International – Photography – Beach – Baby – Bicycling – Running – Business Casual – Business Formal – Fancy Dinner – Motorcycling Editing features to hide items from pre-created packing lists and add custom numbers of items (such as two swimsuits). An average weather estimate (temperature and type of weather like rain or high humidity). Multiple Trips and packing checklists for those trips. Sharing features. Hide checked items feature, allowing you to see only what is remaining to pack. PackPoint Premium Features Custom packing templates that allow you to add new items to the built-in packing lists. Custom activities so that you can create your own custom lists for activities you are participating in, for example, a scuba diving packing list. Integration with TripIt, so that you can view your packing checklist within the TripIt app. Is PackPoint Premium Worth It? PackPoint Premium is worth the money if you are packing unique items. With Premium, you can add personalized items to lists, ensuring you don’t forget to pack them. It’s also worth it if you want to customize the general items that are automatically added. For example, if you want to specify which brand and color of clothing item to pack instead of lists having more general items like “t-shirts.” Due to PackPoint Premium offering integration with TripIt, it will also be worth the money if you use that app and want to store all of your travel information, including your packing list, in one place. Best for Overall Travel: Wanderlog Wanderlog via Apple App Store : Free/$39.99; 4.9/5 stars (19,100 reviews) Wanderlog via Google Play Store : Free/$39.99; 4.6/5 stars (18,800 reviews) How To Create a Packing List With Wanderlog Follow the steps to create a trip, complete with destination and start and end dates. Click the trip you want to create a packing list for then click the plus sign in the bottom right-hand corner and select “Checklist.” You can select “New List” or use one of the pre-made lists Wanderlog offers. In that list, start adding your packing list in the notes section. To make a checklist, put a square bracket checkbox next to each item [ ] and fill it out with an x or another symbol or emoji when each item is packed. You could also create individual lists for different things, such as Carry-On Bag Packing List and Checked-Bag Packing List or Clothing and Toiletries. Pros of Wanderlog Customizable Packing List: Although there are no pre-created packing lists, Wanderlog offers the option to make completely customizable packing lists. This is a useful feature if you are packing unique items or if you want to be specific about what items to pack instead of having generic options like “dress” or “shoes.” Travel Planning and Organization Features: One of the benefits of using Wanderlog as a packing list app is that you get access to many other travel planning features, including budgeting tools, itinerary creation, document storage and activity suggestions. This will be appealing if you want to organize every part of your trip, from what you need to pack to what you’re doing and when you’re doing it. Free to Use: Most of Wanderlog’s features are free to use, with the custom packing lists via notes are 100% free to use. This is a plus for those who want to create customized lists without spending money as most other travel packing list apps only allow you to create custom lists or add custom items for a fee. Cons of Wanderlog Too Many Extra Features: If you only want to build a packing list, Wanderlog will likely have too many extra features. The user experience will be better with an app that is solely for creating packing lists without having many other features distracting from your packing list. Notable Features of Wanderlog Itinerary Creation One of the primary features of Wanderlog is detailed, day-by-day travel itinerary creation. You can email travel confirmations from your email account to the app to sync with your itinerary, add all your activities (including those found within the app’s activity suggestion tools), and view your itinerary on a map. This feature is not only helpful for staying organized when planning for your trip but also helps with packing, as you can easily see all the activities you’ll be enjoying on your trip, allowing you to pack exactly what you need. Activity Suggestions You can search for various activity ideas within the Wanderlog app once you have added your destination(s). There are many categories to choose from, including popular attractions, restaurants and bars, and outdoor activities. You can even search for accommodation options. Once you’ve discovered activities you’d like to try, simply click to add them to your itinerary. Curated guides are also created if you’re looking for inspiration on where to travel to or want to follow pre-created itineraries for cities you’re visiting. This feature can be helpful for packing as you can finalize your itinerary as much as possible with all the activities you want to try before leaving for the trip. By knowing what activities you’ll be doing each day, you can better pack all the items you will need without having to buy things when you arrive. Notes and Lists It’s super easy to add lists and notes to your trip to help you remember things, such as what to pack. Within notes, you can create a fully custom packing list with all the items you need to pack. As you remember things to pack, simply add them to your packing list note. Best of all, all customizations to your packing list are free (which isn’t the case with most other packing apps). Other Travel Planning Features Along with the above features, you can access various other travel planning and organization tools in the Wanderlog app, including: Budgeting tools Travel documentation forwarding from email Road trip route planning Hotel booking via Kayak Special travel deals and promos Trip sharing features Is Wanderlog Free? Wanderlog is free to use and can be accessed via web browser and on iOS or Android devices. The free plan includes many helpful features, such as itinerary creation, budgeting tools, and travel notes like packing lists. You can also gain extra features by purchasing Wanderlog Pro, starting at $39.99 per year. Wanderlog Features: Free Add unlimited places and activity suggestions Collaboration and sharing features Import booking confirmations like flights, hotels, and car rentals Smart recommendations Itinerary and map view Travel budgeting tools Wanderlog Pro Features: $39.99/year Offline access to itineraries and maps Exporting of maps to Google Maps Auto scanning of travel confirmations from Gmail Unlimited attachments Road trip route optimization Flight and car rental deals Dark mode AI assistance Chrome extension map What Does Wanderlog Do? Wanderlog is a travel planning tool that can help you to organize upcoming trips by creating itineraries, tracking reservations, managing expenses, and more. The travel planning app allows collaboration with others, integrates maps, and offers custom day-by-day itineraries, among many other features. Users can also import bookings and track trip costs, making it a streamlined solution for planning and managing upcoming trips. Best for Specialty and Custom Packing Lists: Packr Packr via Apple App Store : Free/$3.49 per month/$24.99 per year/$34.99 lifetime 4.6/5 stars (6,300 reviews). Packr is only available for iOS and can’t be used with Android devices. Image Courtesy of Packr via Apple App Store How To Create a Packing List With Packr Add your destination (multiple destinations can be added with a Packr Premium account), trip start and end dates, and gender. Select accommodation type, transportation you will be using, and activities/packing categories. These categories include: – Essentials – Clothes – Toiletries – International – Beach – Working – Cycling – Formal Dinner – Golf – Gym – Hiking – Photography – Music Festival – Swimming – Winter Sports – To-Do – Baby Select if you will be doing laundry or not on your trip. With Packr Premium, you also have the option to create packing lists for multiple travelers. Click “Create Trip” to generate your packing list based on the above-entered information. The high and low temperatures and type of weather for each day of your trip will also be displayed at the top of your packing list page. To remove items from the pre-created packing lists, swipe them left and click the trashcan icon. To mark things as packed, click the check circle. To add multiple items to your packing list, press the plus sign and then add the number of items you need. To add a new item to the categorized lists, write the name of the item in the “Add Item…” box and click the plus sign. To share the list, select the three dots in the upper right-hand corner, click “Share Trip,” then choose if you want the person with the link to only view the list or be able to edit it. Finally, click “Share” and choose how to share, including via SMS, WhatsApp, and email. You also have the option to add “Quick Lists.” When creating a Quick List, you follow the same steps as above but leave out adding a destination or start and end dates. This packing list is useful if you’re traveling to multiple places but don’t have a premium account or if you need a packing list for something other than a trip. Pros of Packr Activity-Based Packing Lists: You can choose from 17 different categories with specialized items, including hiking, beach, and essentials, allowing you to have packing list items for every activity on your trip. Customizable Lists: Unlike some of the other packing list apps on this list, Packr allows you to add your own items to lists with a free account. This is useful if you have things to pack which aren’t commonly on pre-created packing lists. You can also specify items instead of being stuck with generalizations like t-shirts, shorts, dresses, etc. making remembering the exact items you want to pack easier. Weather Integration: The high and low temperatures for each day of your trip, plus the most likely type of weather (rain, cloudy, sunny, etc.) are displayed at the top of your packing list. This feature helps you customize what to pack based on predicted weather. The weather also updates as more forecast information becomes available, allowing you to have the most accurate information when packing for your trip. Additional Features If Needed: Packr’s paid-for features include integration with TripIt, personalized packing lists, multiple destinations connected to one packing list, and family mode which allows you to create a packing list for multiple travelers. The premium version also has no in-app ads. Cons of Packr Not Available for Android: If you have an Android device, you won’t be able to use Packr, eliminating it as an option for an app packing list for many. In-App Ads: If you have the free version, there are ads that show up quite frequently and it’s not overly user-friendly to remove these ads to get back to the packing list. Single Person Packing Lists: Without paying for Packr Premium, you can only create a packing list for one person. This can be limiting if you are a couple or family who needs to create packing lists for the entire group. No Pack Light Option: Packr’s pre-created lists cover everything you need for each day of your trip with no option to create a list that repeats items. If you want to pack light and re-wear pieces and/or have access to laundry during your trip, you’ll likely end up with a pre-created packing list with too many items. However, with the newly added number of items buttons, you can reduce quantities of essentials once a list is created to generate a lighter packing list. Notable Features of Packr Essentials Packing Lists Packr includes pre-built lists with common items like clothes, toiletries, and miscellaneous essentials (often things you would pack in a carry-on like electronics, medication, and hand sanitizer). These are a great base for anyone creating a packing list as the essentials lists feature the bulk of what you’ll need to pack no matter your type of trip. Specialty Packing Lists On top of these general “suitable for every trip” lists, Packr has specialty packing lists for different activities and types of travel. These include: Working International Cycling Golf Hiking Photography Winter Sports Formal Dinner Beach Gym Music Festival Swimming Baby You can also add a to-do list which has common tasks you’ll need to complete before leaving home, such as turning off the lights, closing windows, and watering plants. Weather Information Once your trip location and dates are added, you’ll get weather predictions for each day. This includes a high and low temperature and the general weather for the day (rainy, sunny, cloudy, etc.) Seeing the weather within the app can help finalize your packing list and remind you to pack items you may otherwise forget, such as a raincoat and umbrella if a few days will be wet. Nearby Attractions If you’ve added a destination when creating the packing list, you can click “Nearby Attractions” at the bottom of the packing list screen to see activity suggestions. These are all linked to Get Your Guide. When you click on an activity, you’ll be directed to the Get Your Guide website to learn more and book tickets if desired. While this feature doesn’t optimize your packing list, it’s a useful way to find additional things to do during your trip. If you book something, that activity may need additional clothing or other items that you can add to your packing list. What Is the Packr App? Packr is a packing list app that creates packing checklists to use for all types of travel. You can access pre-created lists with essential items and lists for activities and certain types of travel like beach vacations, work trips, and snow sports holidays. There is also a Premium paid-for version with added features. Packr Free Features Packing list creation Weather information Nearby attractions Packr Premium Features: $3.49 per month/$24.99 per year/$34.99 lifetime Editable packing lists Family mode to create packing lists for multiple people Share features No ads Device synchronization across all Apple devices Best for Detailed Packing Lists: Packing Pro Packing Pro via Apple App Store : $3.99 lifetime 4.8/5 stars (127 reviews) Packing Pro is not available for Android devices. Image Courtesy of Packing Pro via Apple App Store How To Create a Packing List With Packing Pro Use the Expert List Assistant to generate a new packing list. You can input details like the number of adults, children, destination, and trip length to personalize the list as much as possible. Once generated, the list can be fully customized and you have the option to add or remove items from a master catalog of over 800 items. As you pack, check off items and track remaining tasks. You can also adjust quantities of items on your packing list based on the length of your trip and if you will be able to wash or re-wear items. You can also select to save your list as a template for future trips, saving time when organizing for future traveling. Pros of Packing Pro Full Customization: The app offers unparalleled customization. You can create, modify, and reorder categories and items, and even customize lists based on individual needs like family travel, solo travel, or business trips. There are master catalogs within the app that feature over 800 commonly packed and specialty items from which you can pick and choose what you’d like on your packing list. Multi Traveler Lists: As mentioned, Packing Pro allows you to create multiple traveler lists. This includes lists for couples, for families with any number of kids, and even pets! This feature will come in super useful for anyone organizing packing for their whole group. The pet option is also quite unique and is ideal for those traveling with furry friends who need many of their own items packed, including crucial travel documentation if flying or crossing borders. Luggage Weight Calculation: If you’re looking to travel light or often pack over the allowable weight limit, Packing Pro’s luggage weight estimation tool is a very useful feature. While not exact, it offers a great estimate of luggage weight based on what is on your packing list allowing you to remove items before packing them (and having the hassle of removing them later!) This feature isn’t available with many other packing list apps either. Download to CSV: Another feature not offered by many other packing list apps is the option to download your packing list as a CSV file. This allows for offline access and even more customization, plus the ability to share the list via multiple platforms. Cons of Packing Pro Requires Manual Input: Although the app provides a vast master catalog and pre-built lists, there is still a lot of manual work to fully personalize the lists. For frequent travelers, this isn’t a huge downside, but for those who only travel occasionally, it may feel cumbersome, especially as other travel packing list apps don’t require as much set-up or manual input. Some say the interface design is also not very visually appealing. No Free Version: Packing Pro can only be used for a fee. Despite being affordable at only $3.99, this will be a major drawback for those looking for a free packing list app. No Android Version: As the app is currently only available for iOS devices, those with Android devices will need to opt for a different packing list app. Notable Features of Packing Pro Packing Lists With Over 800 Items You can add things to your packing list from a catalog of over 800 items, ensuring everything you need to pack can be added to your list. You can also create lists for multiple travelers, including families. iCloud Sync Packing Pro automatically syncs across all your devices, ensuring you always have access to your packing lists. This is particularly useful when switching between devices mid-trip​. Expert List Assistant One standout feature is the ability to generate a list based on details such as destination, temperature, and trip duration. This automation makes the list creation process quick and smart​ Sharing and Backup Packing Pro makes sharing lists easy with options to email, AirDrop, or save to Dropbox. It’s perfect for group trips where you want everyone to be on the same page​ Is Packing Pro Free? Packing Pro is one of the few packing list apps that does not have a free version. The app costs $3.99 to download via the Apple App Store and is not available for Android or desktop use. Best for Multiple Traveler Packing Lists: Packtor Image Courtesy of Packtor Packtor is not available for iOS in the Apple App Store or for Android in the Google Play Store in the U.S. It can be used via desktop for free with no paid-for features available. How To Create a Packing List With Packtor Select your gender if creating a list for yourself or you have the option to choose “Couple” or “Family.” With the family option, you can add how many babies and children will be traveling. Add destination, trip length, and a name for your packing list. Next, select the climate of your destination, whether your accommodation is a hotel or hostel, and whether your trip is a “holiday” or “backpacking.” You also have the option to choose to “pack extra light” which will create a packing list with minimal items. Based on what you enter on the first two pages, a packing list will be created with things commonly needed for a trip like yours. The packing list is also split into categories, including: – Clothes – Gear (covers things like sunglasses, backpack, and eye mask) – Electronics – Washbag (toiletries) – Documents – First-Aid Kit At the top of the page with the packing list, you will also receive a “To-Do” checklist which includes common tasks to complete before leaving for a trip. Things to do include watering plants, unplugging or switching off devices, and taking out the trash. Once the automated list is created, you can remove things you don’t want to pack by hovering over the item and clicking the trashcan icon. You can also re-order the list by hovering over the items you want to move, clicking the re-organize button and moving it up or down. To mark things as for your carry-on bag, hover over the item and click the hand icon. This item will not be moved to a new list, but the hand icon will remain next to the item, so you remember to add it to your carry-on bag. To add your own items to the packing list, go to the bottom of the category of the list you want to add the item to and write the name of the item before clicking the plus sign. You can also create a new category of list (for example, if you want a specific carry-on packing list instead of just using the icon tool). To do this, go to the bottom of the packing list page, write the name of your category in the “New Category” box and click the plus icon. You can save the list to return to later by clicking “Save List” at the top of the packing list. However, you’ll have to create an account via your email address to do that. Once an account is created, you can share the list via email. An account also means you can access your packing list again to reuse it or customize it for a new trip. Lastly, having an account allows you can see what percent of your packing is complete, with the percentage updating each time you check off an item. Pros of Packtor Easy to Use: Packtor is very straightforward to use and has a user-friendly interface. It’s also easy to add and remove things from lists and add your own categorized lists. Lots of Personalization Options: As mentioned, it’s super easy to add and remove things from pre-created lists and to add your own custom categories of lists. This level of customization is a paid-for feature with many other packing list apps. If you want a high level of customization to ensure everything you want to pack is covered and you don’t forget anything, Packtor is one of the best packing list apps to try. Can Build Multiple Traveler Packing Lists: This packing list app allows you to create a list for solo travelers but also comes with the option to generate a packing checklist for a couple or family. With the family option, you can add the number of babies and/or children. This is a useful feature for those wanting to create a travel packing list for their whole group and is especially helpful for families who will need to keep track of what to pack for their kids as well as themselves. Sharing and Saving Tools: Packtor allows you to save your list and share it with others. This is convenient if you want the packing list on multiple devices and if you have created a list for multiple people to use. Cons of Packtor Desktop Only: Packtor cannot currently be downloaded as an app for iOS or Android. You can use the website on your phone but the functionality is not as good as in an app. You will also need an internet connection to use Packtor unless you print the list. No Additional Travel Planning Tools: Packtor is quite basic and only includes travel checklists. There are no additional travel planning or organization tools, such as itinerary creation, budgeting tools, or activity idea suggestions. This will lessen the appeal of the packing list app for anyone who wants more organization tools in one app along with a packing checklist. Doesn’t Integrate With Other Apps: Unlike some of the packing list apps on this list, Packtor doesn’t integrate with travel planning tools that have additional features, such as TripIt. Therefore, you would have to switch between Packtor and a more in-depth travel planning app if wanting to use both. No Weather Information: Again, unlike many other packing list apps, Packtor doesn’t offer information on what the weather will be like each day of your trip, meaning you’ll have to look this up via a third party platform. Packtor Notable Features Packing List Creation Packtor’s primary feature is packing list creation. These packing lists are generated based on: Gender (with couple and family options) Destination and climate of the destination Duration of trip Travel type: holiday, backpacking, city trip, business trip, winter sports, or trekking There is also a pack light option. Once created, you can add and remove list items from the pre-generated packing lists and even create your own packing list, such as a carry-on bag packing list with everything you need. A handy to-do list before leaving for the trip, with checklist items like watering plants and turning off heat and electricity, is also generated. Multiple Traveler Packing Lists Unlike many other travel packing list apps, you can create multiple traveler lists for free with Packtor. You can pack as a couple or as a family, with the latter option including two adults and a customizable number of babies and children. Packing List Customization Packtor offers customization features for free. You can easily add and remove list items to pre-generated lists and create brand new lists with personalized categories (list names) and items. This is a great feature for anyone that knows exactly what they want to pack and simply wants an easy to use checklist to cross-reference when packing. Save and Share Features Once you create an account for free, you can save your packing list to access it whenever you like and gain access to the percent of packing complete feature. By saving your packing list to your account, you can also use it again for another trip (customizing it as needed). You can also share your packing list via email. This is especially useful if you have created a multi-traveler list and want to share it with your travel partner. Percent of Packing Complete Another feature some of the other best packing lists apps lack that Packtor offers is a percent of packing complete toolbar. As you check things as packed on your packing list, you’ll be able to see what percent of total items is left to pack. This helps a lot with time management, making it easy to see how close you are to having your bag fully packed and ready to go. Packing list Q&A What Is the 5-4-3-2-1 Rule for Packing? The 5-4-3-2-1 Rule is a minimalist packing strategy designed to help you pack efficiently and avoid overpacking for trips. The numbers revolve around the number of items to pack in five common clothing categories: tops, pants/bottoms, shoes, accessories, and an outer layer. Some variations also include one or two dresses in place of accessories or an outer layer. The idea is to limit the number of items you bring by focusing on essentials and mixing and matching pieces. Here’s how it works: 5 Tops : Pack five tops, like t-shirts, blouses, or casual shirts. Choose versatile options that can be dressed up or down. 4 Bottoms : Pack four bottoms, such as jeans, shorts, skirts, or pants. Select neutral colors that match well with your tops. 3 Pairs of Shoes : Limit yourself to three pairs of shoes: one comfortable pair for walking, one casual pair, and one for formal occasions or special activities. 2 Accessories : Choose two accessories, like a hat, scarf, or jewelry, that can enhance your outfits without taking up much space. 1 Outer Layer : Bring one outer layer, like a jacket or sweater, depending on the weather and destination. As mentioned, you could switch one outer layer or one to two accessories with one or two dresses if this works better for your style and travel plans. How Do You Start a Packing List? To create a packing list , first consider all the essentials you need to pack. This includes essential clothing, toiletries, and electronics. It’s a good idea to break your packing list into categories as well, such as clothing, toiletries, and things you want in your carry-on bag. Once you have an essentials list, you can start adding speciality items and items unique to your travel plans. Using a packing lists app is also a great idea to help you start your packing list. Many apps feature pre-created lists complete with common essentials and items packed for different activities like business trips or snow sports holidays. With a base list already created via a packing list app, it’s much easier to create a personalized list, adding and removing items from the base list as you go. Is There an App That Helps You Pack? Yes, there are multiple packing list apps that can help you create a packing list. These apps include pre-created packing lists, including those for specialty activities like hiking or business travel. Some of the best packing list apps available to use include Packing Pro, Packr, and PackPoint. summary: Progress in plant-level operations aligns with recent momentum in commercial strategy and offtake discussions HESPERIA, Calif., Oct. 21, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — 5E Advanced Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: FEAM) (ASX: 5EA)…
body_text: Progress in plant-level operations aligns with recent momentum in commercial strategy and offtake discussions HESPERIA, Calif., Oct. 21, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — 5E Advanced Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: FEAM) (ASX: 5EA) (“5E” or the “Company”), a boron and lithium company with U.S. government Critical Infrastructure designation for its 5E Boron Americas Complex, is pleased to report positive progress at the Company’s Small-Scale Facility (“SSF”). Highlights: Operational focus and rigor at the 5E Boron Americas complex have improved production rates, overall product quality, and consistency Improved operating rates have driven an increase in calcium content, expanding 5E’s commercial optionality regarding byproduct marketing Entered into a definitive agreement with the California Alternative Energy and Advanced Transportation Financing Authority regarding a tax assistance program for capital equipment related to the production of lithium carbonate, with savings potential of nearly $900,000 Paul Weibel, Chief Executive Officer of 5E Advanced Materials, commented, “We are increasingly encouraged by the improvements to our operational performance as we continue to see positive progress at the plant level with solid data points across both our production rates and product quality. We have overcome initial maintenance headwinds and early-stage growing pains, as our operations team has developed innovative solutions to work through challenges and continuously improve processes. The positive progress at the facility plays well alongside the expanding level of discussions we are having with various potential customers as we look to enter offtake commitments and advance 5E’s commercial strategy.” Operations Update Production rates at the Company’s 5E Boron Americas Complex have steadied and are currently maintained at one short ton per day with continuous improvement at the facility. The operations team has successfully programmed crystallization to operate in automatic mode such that distillation occurs based on feed concentration, improving both boric acid consistency and quality. Recently, the facility’s belt filter spray nozzle systems were optimized to maintain sulfur content below 100 ppm, exceeding customer specifications. The Company expects to begin removing metal salts and producing gypsum in the near term as calcium levels and metal salts have lagged boric acid leach rates. Calcium content has now increased to greater than 20,000 ppm, necessitating the production of a calcium-based by-product. As the Company assesses operating expenses and commercial scale engineering, the recovery solution after removing the calcium is expected to reinforce the confidence levels of solution feed profiles that inform raw material utilizations that drive OPEX. The Company continues to evaluate calcium chloride as a potential byproduct and has tested and produced highly concentrated samples (38% Ca) of solution that are representative of what could be produced on a commercial scale. New Tax Exclusion On October 16th, the Company entered into a definitive agreement with the California Alternative Energy and Advanced Transportation Financing Authority (“CAEATFA”) as part of the Sales and Use Tax Exclusion Program (the “Program”). California’s Department of Tax and Fee Administration administers a use tax of 7.75% on capital equipment. Under the Program, assistance is provided by CAEATFA such that any capital equipment attributable to lithium carbonate production is exempt from use tax, up to a limit of $11,473,423. The Agreement could potentially save the Company approximately $889,000 in capital costs. About 5E Advanced Materials, Inc. 5E Advanced Materials, Inc. (Nasdaq: FEAM) (ASX: 5EA) is focused on becoming a vertically integrated global leader and supplier of boron specialty and advanced materials, complemented by lithium co-product production. The Company’s mission is to become a supplier of these critical materials to industries addressing global decarbonization, food and domestic security. Boron and lithium products will target applications in the fields of electric transportation, clean energy infrastructure, such as solar and wind power, fertilizers, and domestic security. The business strategy and objectives are to develop capabilities ranging from upstream extraction and product sales of boric acid, lithium carbonate and potentially other co-products, to downstream boron advanced material processing and development. The business is based on the Company’s large domestic boron and lithium resource, which is located in Southern California and designated as Critical Infrastructure by the Department of Homeland Security’s Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. title: Landstar is Recognized with National Safety Council Award
summary: The National Safety Council (NSC) recognized Landstar Transportation Logistics, Inc. for “Remarkable Results” in the organization’s awards for Excellence in Driver Safety Training.
body_text: The National Safety Council (NSC) recognized Landstar Transportation Logistics, Inc. for “Remarkable Results” in the organization’s awards for Excellence in Driver Safety Training for “leading in their field in building safer drivers.” The Remarkable Results award, under the Professional Truck Driver – Online category, means between 5,000-9,999 commercial motor vehicle drivers completed the NSC’s Defensive Driving Course online in 2023. Independent owner-operators leased to Landstar complete the NSC’s online Defensive Driving Course as part of Landstar’s orientation and qualification process. The NSC’s 2024 award was mentioned on Landstar’s Safety Thursday Conference Call in September by guest speaker Ryan Pietzsch, NSC driver safety program technical consultant. “I want to thank you all for all you do to support NSC,” said Pietzsch. “And to congratulate Landstar, all of you, for your outstanding safety records and activities.” Just days before, Landstar Vice President of Safety and Compliance Shelly Seaton accepted the award in Orlando, Florida, while attending the Defensive Driving Courses International Advisory Committee annual meeting during the NSC’s 2024 Safety Congress & Expo. The Expo event also marked the 60th anniversary of the National Safety Council’s first defensive driving course. “While a lot has changed in the 60 years since the NSC launched our first-of-its-kind defensive driving course, the heart of the program remains the same – to save lives on our roads,” said Lorraine Martin, NSC President and CEO in a news release. “Leaders like the 2024 Defensive Driving Course Award recipients set the standard for teaching and exercising safety on the road. Thanks to them we are making our roadways safer for everyone.” According to the organization, the National Safety Council has been America’s leading nonprofit safety advocate for 110 years.

title: The Power of UX Writing and Microcopy: A Guide for Aspiring UX Writers
summary: In today's digital world, where apps, websites, and services are competing for user attention, easy interaction and clear communication are key. body_text: In today's digital world, where apps, websites, and services are competing for user attention, easy interaction and clear communication are key. That’s where UX writing and microcopy come in! UX writing goes beyond just words; it shapes how users interact with a product and ensures that every step is intuitive, pleasant, and efficient. Microcopy, on the other hand, comprises those small, carefully chosen words or phrases that can make a world of difference to users' perception and engagement. If you're an aspiring UX writer or simply looking for UX online courses to increase your skillset, exploring the importance of UX writing and developing the necessary skills to create effective microcopy is essential. This article will guide you through the fundamentals of UX writing, explore the best practices for crafting impactful microcopy, and help you break into the industry. UX Writing: A Key Design Too What is UX Writing? UX writing is the words people see and interact with on apps and websites. This type of writing focuses on making sure that every button, menu, or message helps people use the product smoothly and understand what to do next. The goal is to make the experience clear, friendly, and easy, so people don't get confused or frustrated. Good UX writing keeps things simple, using everyday language to guide users and help them get what they need without any hassle. UX writing is not just about crafting sentences; it's about designing experiences with words. Everything a user sees on the screen — buttons, menus, notifications, forms, and error messages — requires carefully thought-out language to help them move through their journey effortlessly. Think of UX writing as a design tool. Just like images, layout, and function are designed to solve a problem, the words on the screen are used to eliminate confusion, build trust, and lead users toward their goals. Why UX Writing Matters The role of UX writing becomes more and more important as digital products continue to evolve. While sleek designs and smooth navigation are important, without clear communication, users can quickly become frustrated and abandon the experience. Good UX writing creates a seamless, intuitive experience, where users don’t need to think too hard or second-guess their actions. It also builds trust by setting the right expectations and providing the right information at the right time. Take, for example, the microcopy on a "Submit" button. Changing this to "Create Your Account" tells users exactly what will happen when they click it — eliminating any guesswork. Similarly, well-crafted error messages that offer solutions rather than just stating "Something went wrong" can help prevent user frustration and drop-off rates. UX writing is a key part of the design process, working alongside visual and interaction designers to create user-friendly interfaces. Microcopy: The Small Words That Make a Big Difference Microcopy are the small pieces of text that appear on user interfaces — labels, tooltips, error messages, button text, and prompts. While they may not seem that important , these tiny bits of copy play a huge role in shaping the user experience. Microcopy can calm a frustrated user, build trust, clarify complex steps, and even bring a smile to someone’s face during an otherwise mundane process. Why Microcopy is Essential Good microcopy is important because it has a direct impact on user behavior. It helps users complete tasks quickly and without confusion. Clear, concise, and action-oriented language can guide users and reduce how much they need to think when using a product like an app. Microcopy can also express a brand's personality and tone, making the product more relatable and memorable. For instance, consider the friendly "Oops! Looks like you missed a field" instead of the bland "Error." The first version is more playful and gives users more information about what wrong s. Microcopy is all about understanding user pain points and providing help at important moments. Best Practices in UX Writing and Microcopy Let’s look at some of the best practices for crafting effective UX writing and microcopy that enhance user experience: 1. Be Clear and Concise One of the core principles of UX writing is clarity. Users don’t have time to try to understand complex instructions or vague language. Your copy needs to be straightforward and hard to misinterpret. Every word should serve a purpose — if it doesn’t, remove it. Keep sentences short, actionable, and direct. For example, instead of saying, "Please enter your information in the fields provided," say, "Enter your details." 2. Guide Users at Every Step UX writing is there to help users navigate through an interface. Think about what they need to know at every stage of the journey and provide the right instructions at the right time. Your microcopy should anticipate user questions or concerns and address them proactively. For instance, if users need to create a password, include password requirements upfront instead of waiting until they make a mistake. A line like, “Use at least 8 characters, with 1 number and 1 symbol” can prevent errors and frustration. 3. Match the Tone to the Brand and Audience The tone of your UX writing should reflect the brand’s personality and the audience's expectations. Are you writing for a playful mobile game app or a serious financial services website? Your microcopy should align with the overall voice and feel of the brand. While keeping it professional and straightforward is important, don't be afraid to infuse a bit of personality, especially if it adds to the experience. For example, Slack is known for its friendly, approachable tone. Its UX writing includes playful microcopy like, “Oops, that didn’t work. Want to try again?” instead of formal error messages. This human touch makes the experience more enjoyable for users. 4. Provide Solutions, Not Just Problems When something goes wrong, users need more than just an error message. Instead of vague messages like "Invalid input," tell users what they need to do next to fix the issue. For example, “Invalid email format. Please use a format like name@example.com” is more helpful than simply “Invalid email.” This approach reduces user frustration and improves the likelihood that users will complete the task successfully. 5. Use Microcopy to Build Trust Microcopy can play a significant role in building trust with your users. When dealing with sensitive information, such as personal data or payment details, reassure users that their information is secure. You can use microcopy to inform users that their data is protected, which helps reduce their concerns. For example, a microcopy message near a payment form can say, “Your payment is secure and encrypted with 256-bit SSL.” Top Examples of UX Writing and Microcopy Many successful brands have set the bar high for UX writing and microcopy. Here are some notable examples: Google’s Search Experience: Google’s search results page uses simple yet powerful microcopy to enhance user experience. The use of suggestions like “Did you mean…” helps users refine their search without feeling like they’ve made a mistake. This improves the search experience and prevents frustration. Airbnb’s Host Onboarding: Airbnb does an excellent job of guiding users through the process of becoming a host. Clear and friendly UX writing breaks down complex steps, and microcopy helps reduce concerns by answering common questions right where they arise. Mailchimp’s Error Messaging: Mailchimp is well-known for its playful yet informative tone. Their error messages are designed to make users smile, even when something goes wrong. For example, "Looks like you forgot to add an email address. Let's fix that!" is much more user-friendly than a generic error message. Breaking into UX Writing: Skills and Steps Breaking into UX writing requires a blend of writing proficiency, design thinking, and user empathy. Here’s how to get started: 1. Develop Your Writing Skills UX writing is different from traditional copywriting . You need to focus on creating concise, clear, and actionable copy that aligns with user needs. Start by honing your writing skills, especially in crafting microcopy. Consider taking specialized courses in UX writing or copywriting to enhance your skills, like Design Masterclass’s UX Writing for UX Designers . 2. Learn Design Thinking UX writing is part of the design process, so it’s essential to understand how design thinking works. Familiarize yourself with user-centered design principles and how copy fits into the broader user experience. You can learn design thinking through various UX courses available online. Bootcamps like Avocademy ’s offer a wide variety of UX online courses that can help you learn how design thinking works. 3. Build a Portfolio Once you've honed your writing and design skills, start building a portfolio that demonstrates your ability to create effective UX copy. Include case studies that show how your microcopy improved user experiences or solved user pain points. Portfolios are essential for showcasing your work to potential employers. The best UX design courses should include portfolio help so if you’re looking for an UX online course, this is something to look out for! 4. Stay Updated on UX Trends UX writing is constantly evolving with new tools, trends, and best practices. Keep learning with UX online courses and stay current on what’s happening in the industry. Follow UX blogs , attend webinars, and connect with other UX professionals to share insights and experiences. Conclusion: Mastering UX Writing and Microcopy UX writing and microcopy may seem like small pieces of the design puzzle, but they have a big impact on user experience. By creating clear, concise, and user-centered copy, you can guide users through digital interfaces effortlessly and make their interactions more enjoyable. For aspiring UX writers, developing these skills is key to breaking into the industry and creating memorable digital experiences. Start by mastering the basics, building a strong portfolio, and continuously learning from the best examples of UX writing and microcopy. With the right skills, you can not only improve user experiences but also help shape the future of digital products. title: CellChorus and UH Awarded $2.5 Million STTR — CellChorus
summary: The National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) of the NIH has awarded CellChorus and the University of Houston an STTR Fast-Track grant to advance the development of the Time-lapse Imaging Microscopy In Nanowell Grids™ (TIMING™) platform for dynamic single-cell analysis.
body_text: CellChorus and University of Houston Awarded $2.5 million STTR Fast-Track grant for innovations in A.I. Up to $2.5 million in funding from the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences at the NIH will be used to develop an integrated computer vision system for label-free analysis and focus restoration PRESS RELEASE HOUSTON, Texas — October 7, 2024. CellChorus®, the dynamic single-cell analysis company™, and the University of Houston today announced that the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS) of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) has awarded CellChorus and the University of Houston a Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Fast-Track grant to advance the development of the Time-lapse Imaging Microscopy In Nanowell Grids™ (TIMING™) platform for dynamic single-cell analysis with label-free analysis. A two-year $2.1 million Phase II grant will begin after predetermined milestones are achieved under a $350,000 Phase I grant that is underway. TIMING assays are powerful and versatile high-throughput in vitro assays that quantitatively profile cell-cell interactions on a large scale, especially the interactions of immune cells with target cells. The platform has demonstrated value in applications including designing novel therapies, selecting lead candidates for clinical trials, predicting response, and evaluating potency and viability of manufactured cells in immuno-oncology. “By combining AI, microscale manufacturing, and advanced microscopy, the TIMING platform yields deep insight into cellular behaviors that directly impact human disease and new classes of therapeutics,” said Rebecca Berdeaux, Ph.D., Chief Scientific Officer at CellChorus. “The generous support of NCATS enables our development of computational tools that will ultimately integrate single-cell dynamic functional analysis of cell behavior with intracellular signaling events.” This STTR award will support the development of a scalable integrated software system capable of dynamic single-cell analysis on cells that are not fluorescently labeled. To increase the breadth of applications for translational medicine and other applications, there is a compelling need to make fluorescence channels available to integrate additional investigational probes concurrently. This label-free analysis will be based on new artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models trained on tens of millions of images of cells and be optimized for fast, high-throughput single cell analysis by any customer without computational science backgrounds. “This is an opportunity to leverage artificial intelligence methods for advancing the life sciences,” said Badri Roysam, D.Sc., Hugh Roy and Lillie Cranz Cullen University Professor at the University of Houston. “We are especially excited about its applications to advancing cell-based immunotherapy to treat cancer and other diseases.” The CellChorus TIMING platform is available through a commercial service in the CellChorus Innovation Lab located in Houston, Texas. Data from TIMING assays have been featured in more than 20 peer-reviewed papers across a range of cell types and therapeutic areas. Industry leaders have leveraged TIMING data in many different applications, including research, preclinical development, clinical development, manufacturing analytics, and the identification of biomarkers predictive of patient response. In addition to providing data on cellular movement, morphology, interactions, killing, survival and subcellular activity over time, the TIMING platform can provide data on individual cell phenotype and biomolecule secretion. Individual cells of interest can be retrieved for linked downstream analysis such as transcriptional or proteomic profiling. This grant is provided by the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences of the National Institutes of Health under Award Number 1R42TR005299. The content of this release is solely the responsibility of the authors and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health. About CellChorus CellChorus® is the leader in applying artificial intelligence to quantify the function and performance of cells over time to improve the development and delivery of novel therapies that improve patient care. The company applies Time-lapse Imaging Microscopy In Nanowell Grids™ (TIMING™) with neural network-based detection to identify how cells move, activate, kill, and survive at single-cell resolution. The patent-protected platform can link TIMING data and insights with information from other analysis modalities such as single-cell RNA sequencing to provide a comprehensive understanding of cellular function, state and phenotype. title: 4 things to know about our acquisition of Silk Road Medical
summary: This acquisition will enable us to reach more of the millions of people at risk of stroke around the world. Learn how.
body_text: As the president of the Vascular group in the Peripheral Interventions business, Cat Jennings oversees the development of minimally invasive treatments for conditions that affect the blood vessels, such as peripheral artery disease (PAD), and diseases of the veins, like deep vein thrombosis. “Our mission is to be the best peripheral company in the world, and for the world,” says Jennings. One of the most recent ways Jennings’s team is working toward this ambitious goal is through the acquisition of Silk Road Medical. She explains how this development will enable Boston Scientific to reach even more of the millions of people at risk of stroke around the world each year. What is Silk Road Medical known for? To me, the Silk Road Medical story is really the story of stroke prevention. Carotid artery disease affects approximately four million patients in the U.S., with 400,000 new cases diagnosed each year, and is one of the leading causes of stroke.i This condition is caused when plaque builds up in the carotid arteries in the neck and a stroke can occur if this buildup stops blood flow or plaque fragments travel to the brain. Treatment options for people with carotid artery disease historically include optimal medical therapy, open surgery (carotid endarterectomy) and transfemoral carotid artery stenting, in which a stent is delivered from the femoral artery in the groin through the abdomen and up to the carotid artery. Seeing the opportunity to uniquely combine the best aspects of these procedures, Silk Road Medical developed a procedure called transcarotid artery revascularization, or TCAR . In a TCAR procedure, a vascular surgeon places a small stent directly into the carotid artery through a small incision in the neck. What’s unique about TCAR is that blood flow is temporarily reversed during the procedure so any bits of plaque that may break off are diverted away from the brain, where they could otherwise cause a stroke. The procedure is less invasive than open surgery, which may require general anesthesia and can be too risky for some patients. Additionally, the TCAR procedure allows for direct access to the carotid arteries, while the transfemoral approach requires entering the body from the groin. That’s a hard path with a lot of anatomy to get through, including the arch of the aorta in the chest, making it a more complicated option. TCAR has among the lowest reported stroke rate of any carotid intervention, making this a wonderful technology for us to bring into our portfolio alongside our other minimally invasive therapies.ii How do you feel it's a good match for Boston Scientific? This acquisition and the TCAR technology allow us to better serve patients because TCAR is much less invasive than the current standard of care surgical procedure, and the results are just as good. It also allows us to provide a better solution for physicians with faster, more predictable procedures. And it's better for the health care system, because TCAR leads to shorter hospital stays, and may lead to fewer complications.iii What plans do you have for the growth of TCAR in the years to come? First, we want to build on the momentum that Silk Road Medical has built in the United States, relying on their unique expertise around the TCAR procedure. There's also a huge opportunity to take this product to other regions around the world. There are so many patients who may benefit from this therapy that don't have access to it, and with the strength of Boston Scientific, we're going to be able to bring that technology to them. What drives you to keep creating new solutions for patients with vascular conditions, whether through the development of new technologies or through acquisitions like this one? I’ve been at Boston Scientific for 20 years. In every level of the organization, I'm surrounded by incredible people who are passionate about the products we develop. I’m proud of all that we’ve accomplished but realize there's so much work to do to help bring even better solutions to physicians and their patients, and that’s what gets me excited about not just the last 20 years, but what the next 20 years hold. title: Expanding Open Access: How Open Source Principles Can Transform Scientific Communication
summary: A panel discussion with Lorena Barba, Rowan Cockett, Karthik Ram and Arfon Smith explores how open source software practices can reshape the way we communicate scientific discoveries. Adopting open source tools and processes could drastically improve scientific communication, especially with the growing complexity and interconnectedness of research data.
body_text: Expanding Open Access: How Open Source Principles Can Transform Scientific Communication rowan - Project Jupyter · October 25, 2024 In a recent panel discussion on open source software as infrastructure for diamond open access Lorena Barba , who is currently the Faculty Director of the GW Open Source Program Office , hosted a discussion between Rowan Cockett , Karthik Ram and Arfon Smith exploring how open source software practices can reshape the way we communicate scientific discoveries. The panel discussion ventured beyond access to published scientific PDFs, envisioning a future where open access is synonymous with open processes, transparent peer review, continuous scientific updates, and collaborative workflows. Drawing on models from open source software communities, the panelists emphasized that open access should include not only the finished research but also the workflows, data, and iterative improvements that lead to those conclusions. Continuous Science: Iterating Towards Understanding ¶ One compelling idea from the panel was the concept of continuous science , which borrows from software’s continuous integration and deployment practices see Cockett et al. , 2024 . Just as software engineers release incremental updates, researchers could share new data, code, and insights continuously, inviting feedback and improvement along the way. Karthik Ram, cofounder of the rOpenSci project and currently a program officer for Open Science at The Navigation Fund , contrasted how we work on software to how we work on science: In software, we don’t wait years working quietly behind the scenes and then make one little release and talk about that release for the next 20 years. We work continuously , and then from time to time when things reach a stable state, we make a release to say, this is our best version of [an idea] at this point in time. Karthik Ram Instead of periodic, static publications, continuous science could enable researchers to decide when they want to announce a major finding or an incremental insight. This approach not only keeps science moving forward but provides more transparency in how research conclusions are reached, enabling others to build on the most current knowledge. Both Lorena Barba and Arfon Smith noted that a key requirement is automation: “Automation allows continuous improvement” with Karthik adding that “we barely have scraped the surface” of what is possible when it comes to applying automation to how science is communicated professionally. The analogy between scientific publishing and software releases is imperfect and non-prescriptive (i.e. scientific research is very different than developing a software product). However, the analogy is illustrative in areas where there is a focus on iterations, smaller changesets and releasing in-progress work as soon as possible to get feedback from peers. Peer Review: Uppercase and lowercase ¶ The conversation highlighted the potential for redefining peer review in a continuous science model. Rowan Cockett differentiated between what he called uppercase and lowercase peer review. Uppercase Peer Review ™ , he explained, is the traditional, formal journal review process, while lowercase peer review resembles the shorter, more dynamic, iterative feedback that open source developers might receive through pull requests or even private collaborative interaction from colleagues. Arfon Smith, founder of the Journal of Open Source Software and currently Director of Product–AI at GitHub, reflected that the JOSS community looked to the best aspects of open-source software collaboration when designing their own peer review process, which has often been hailed as a collaborative, corrective and a refreshingly pleasant experience by JOSS authors and editors. Open source communities have developed roles, playbooks, even ‘dance moves’ to perform continuous improvement in software. Lorena Barba In software, review is completed continuously on smaller changesets, often through pull requests, which can be a model for ongoing scientific critique and collaboration. The largest peer review platform on the planet, I think, is GitHub. Arfon Smith This peer review doesn’t need to happen in a journal (or all on GitHub!); rather, it could be a collaborative, community driven , public process that involves researchers and stakeholders at all levels, reducing the bottleneck of traditional peer review and fostering a more inclusive scientific dialogue. Open Access to the Process , Not Just the PDF ¶ The panelists called for a broader and deeper vision of open access — one that goes beyond the static published article. “It’s not just access to the science or the PDF,” said Lorena Barba, “but access to the process, to the review, to the small changes that lead us closer to the truth.” By embracing open source models, researchers can build on each other’s work with full transparency, from the original data to each analytical step and result, creating a cumulative, public record that others can both verify and extend. Difficult problems that are globally relevant and urgent - like climate change, pandemics, and water security - require us to radically rethink how we publish and work on scientific breakthroughs. A big part of this how we as researchers work, collaborate and share — ensuring that this aligns to the iterative, experimental, self-corrective process of science itself. It is not the current scientific theory (or paper!) that we are proud of, but the scientific process to get to that next idea or breakthrough. Automation and Reproducibility at Scale ¶ Automation plays a critical role in the open source vision of continuous science. By automating repetitive tasks—such as generating PDFs, submission, checking formatting, metadata, references, editorial rules, or ensuring reproducibility of results—researchers can focus more on their actual findings. Today there is an estimated USD$230 million spent on reformatting articles by scientists before publication Clotworthy et al. , 2023 — effort that could certainly be better allocated! Karthik noted that automation also has the potential to “dramatically reduce the cognitive burden on peer review” by automatically validating datasets or checking code, which in turn allows reviewers to focus on interpreting and understanding the science itself. Moving Toward a More Open Research Future ¶ The panelists agreed that adopting open source tools and processes could drastically improve scientific communication, especially with the growing complexity and interconnectedness of research data. As Rowan Cockett noted, “We’re not just looking to improve journals. We need new tools that help scientists communicate complex, reproducible work at scale, in a way that everyone can use.” Open access principles can transform research communication and help set new standards for collaboration, transparency, and reproducibility in science. The future of open access might not only be more open, but fundamentally different — built on the principles of open source to promote continuous improvement, incremental publication, and truly collaborative, global science. Panelists Lorena Barba ¶ Dr. Lorena A. Barba is a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering and international affairs, and the Faculty Director of the GW Open Source Program Office. Her interests include computational fluid dynamics, open science, and computational reproducibility. She has a history of educational innovation and contributions to open education, which has been recognized with several awards. Additionally, she is well known for her leadership in open-source software and science reproducibility. She has been a member of the board of directors of NumFOCUS, founding editor of The Journal of Open Source Software, editor-in-chief of IEEE Computational Science and Engineering, and editor-in-chief of The Journal of Open Source Education. Rowan Cockett ¶ Rowan, CEO and cofounder of Curvenote, a publishing platform for researchers, societies, and institutes, aims to free science from static PDF documents. With a Ph.D. in computational geophysics from UBC, Rowan helped start SimPEG, a simulation and parameter estimation package for geophysical processes. Rowan has won awards for innovative dissemination of research and open-educational resources, including Visible Geology, used by over a million geoscience students. Rowan serves on the steering council for JupyterBook and MyST Markdown, providing open-source tools for scientific content creation and sharing. Karthik Ram ¶ Karthik Ram, currently a program officer for Open Science at The Navigation Fund, previously worked as a research scientist at the University of California, Berkeley, for about 14 years. At Berkeley, he co-founded and directed the rOpenSci project, supporting open and reproducible research, and was the lead principal investigator for the URSSI (US Research Software Sustainability Institute). He also has a PhD in evolution and evolutionary biology from the University of California, Davis. Arfon Smith ¶ Arfon Smith, currently the Director of Product/AI at GitHub, focuses on the Copilot Enterprise product. His professional roles involve helping organizations utilize data effectively and his dedication to open-source software.
